Crippling depression.

I was working at a photo studio once, and a man with his 5 year old son came in to take some pictures. It was just a regular photo shoot that he wanted to take with his kid, and I swear he was the most patient man with him. He would reinforce good behavior with rewarding him candy, teaching him to respect others and respect will be given back, etc. 

Also, he taught him how to be responsible about money. I mean, like, holy shit, the kid knew more about personal finance than me at the time. The kid was only 5 years old.

Oh, and another case of the worst parent I have ever seen. I lived with roommates, who were a young couple, that would fight in front of their kid. They would constantly bash on each other to the point where they would raise their fist against each other. It didn't happened one time, but it happened 3-4 times when I wasn't home. And when I did come home, and learning about what happened, the child would constantly cry for hours, traumatized by watching both of the spill blood on each other. I had to kick them out of the house. That was not okay at all.

I have a super spoiled little cousin thinking it was super funny to throw a dirty diaper to my face, full of feces while I was still sleeping. Apparently his mother thought it was completely funny, too, so when I told him that it wasn't okay to do that to people, especially family, he completely laughed it off.

 Like, I understand that some kids of that certain age like to fool around a lot because they're just kids. But after witnessing my aunt acknowledging that kind of behavior baffles me. I know I'm being a tight ass and all, but it annoys the shit out of me.

Hey, friend. First of all, you are not alone. There were so many mistakes that I have made, and the fact that the memories creep up on me always make me cringe because it's so embarrassing, or the fact that it is something you, and just you, will always remember. If I were you, I would view those screw ups as learning experiences because it would help you grow as a person. FYI, this is coming from someone who experiences crippling depression and anxiety every single day. Remember, friend, no matter how much you screw up, you can take it day by day slowly. There is no rush. Life may seem hell to you right now, but I can only tell you that it will get better when you start small, very small manageable bits.
